bib.title: Bi-Directional Attention Flow for Machine Comprehension

question: How can a reading-comprehension model link a question and a paragraph with attention without summarising the paragraph early into a fixed-size vector?
hypothesis: Memory-less, bi-directional attention whose per-position vectors flow into a modeling layer (instead of being summarised) divides labour between attention and modeling and beats dynamic, uni-directional, summarising attention.
contributions: BiDAF: hierarchical multi-stage architecture (char, word, contextual embeddings) with bi-directional attention flow giving a query-aware context representation without early summarization
State-of-the-art on SQuAD test and CNN/DailyMail cloze test at time of submission
Ablations, embedding visualisations, comparison with a feature-based baseline and error analysis on SQuAD dev

method.summary: Six-layer network: char-CNN and GloVe embeddings through a 2-layer highway network, a BiLSTM contextual layer, a bi-directional attention flow layer (context-to-query and query-to-context from one similarity matrix, fused by concatenation), a 2-layer BiLSTM modeling layer, and a start/end span output layer. Trained from scratch on SQuAD with AdaDelta; output layer swapped for CNN/DailyMail cloze.
method.task: extractive machine comprehension (SQuAD span prediction) and cloze-style reading comprehension (CNN/DailyMail)

datasets.name: SQuAD
datasets.size: more than 100,000 questions; 90k/10k train/dev tuples plus a large hidden test set

datasets.name: CNN
datasets.preprocessing: missing word is an anonymised named entity with random ID; IDs shuffled constantly during test; each article split into 19-word windows around each entity

models.name: BiDAF
models.architecture: char-CNN + GloVe + 2-layer highway, BiLSTM contextual layer, bi-directional attention flow, 2-layer BiLSTM modeling layer, softmax start/end output (extra BiLSTM for end)
models.init_from: GloVe word vectors (fixed, pre-trained); everything else from scratch (inferred: no other init stated)
models.layers: inferred: 2 highway + 1 BiLSTM contextual + 2 BiLSTM modeling + 1 BiLSTM for end index

training.objective: sum of negative log probabilities of true start and end indices, averaged over examples; for cloze, only start loss on summed probability of all instances of the answer entity
training.epochs: 12 (SQuAD); 8 with early stop on validation accuracy (CNN/DailyMail)
training.seq_len: 19-word windows around each entity (cloze); SQuAD paragraph length not stated
training.dropout: 0.2 on CNN, all LSTM layers, and linear transform before answer softmax
training.regularisation: exponential moving average of all weights, decay 0.999, used at test time
training.hardware: single Titan X GPU (SQuAD); eight Titan X GPUs (CNN/DailyMail)
training.seeds: ensemble of 12 training runs with identical architecture and hyper-parameters

other.cloze_changes: p2 omitted from loss; non-entity words masked in final classification layer; RNNs not run across sentence windows

inference.decoding: answer span (k,l), k<=l, maximising p1_k * p2_l, via linear-time dynamic programming
inference.samples: single model; ensemble of 12 runs picks answer with highest sum of confidence scores

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: model credited if answer matches one of the human-written answers

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: weighted average of precision and recall at character level (as printed)

metrics.name: accuracy (cloze)
metrics.definition: fraction of correctly predicted entities on CNN/DailyMail val/test

baselines: Attentive Reader, MemNN, AS Reader, DER Network, Iterative Attention, EpiReader, Stanford AR, GAReader, AoA Reader, ReasoNet (CNN/DailyMail)
eval.protocol: SQuAD test numbers are from the leaderboard as of 6 Dec 2016; ablations are single runs on dev; no significance tests or seed variance reported

evidence.quote: We use a minibatch size of 48 and train for 8 epochs

limits: Ablations are single runs with no variance reported; Table 1b and Table 5 print different dev scores for the same single model (67.7/77.3 vs 68.0/77.3).
SQuAD test rows for IBM Watson and MSRA are unpublished leaderboard entries as of 6 Dec 2016; the state-of-the-art claim has long dated.
Multi-hop attention is left as future work.
LSTM-based and slow (about 20 h on one Titan X); superseded by Transformer and pre-trained models.
Word-level embedding ablation and visualisations are qualitative; conjectures about why (word vs char embeddings, division of labour) are not tested directly.

terms.definition: the attention at each time step is a function of only the query and the context paragraph at the current time step and does not directly depend on the attention at the previous time step
G, a vector per context word fusing the contextual embedding with the attended query (C2Q) and attended context (Q2C) vectors
signifies which query words are most relevant to each context word
signifies which context words have the closest similarity to one of the query words and are hence critical for answering the query
